items.title: E27-S10 Registry fetch + schema validation + cache

labels.name: story
labels.description: Story — a 1–3 day unit with acceptance criteria

items.body:
> **E27-S10 · Registry fetch + schema validation + cache**
> Epic #30 E27 — ACP client & agent panel · Phase 5 · Size M · Wave 11

## Why this story exists
Users should not have to type a command to run an agent. The ACP registry lists 41 agents with how to launch each. This story fetches it, validates it against a vendored schema, caches it with a TTL, falls back to built-in presets offline, and turns each entry into an `AgentSpec`. The registry is untrusted runtime input, so validation is the point.

## Where it fits
- **Layer / crates:** `oxikube_acp::registry` (adapters)
- **Ports & types touched:** `registry.json` (`{version, agents[], extensions[]}`), `AgentSpec { dist: npx | uvx | binary }`, JSON-schema validation, cache with TTL, built-in presets (E27-S12).
- **Epic context:** After S03. It unblocks S11 (launchers use the specs). The registry URL is `https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json`.
- **Project rules that apply:** Treat the registry as untrusted input (research risk: schema churn); adapters depend only on domain + ports; no network at startup (cold start ≤ 400 ms, catalog before any network); no secrets in the cache.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch registry.json, validate against vendored schema, cache with TTL + offline fallback to presets; entries → AgentSpec {dist: npx|uvx|binary}

## Implementation notes (guidance, not contract)
- Fetch `https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json` with the HTTP client already approved for adapters (reqwest is allowed in adapters; check `deny.toml` and `[workspace.dependencies]`). Use ETag or `If-None-Match` if the CDN supports it, and a request timeout.
- Vendor the registry JSON schema under `crates/adapters/oxikube_acp/schema/` and validate before use. Which validator crate to use is not in the research docs; pick a maintained one and check `cargo deny`. Log which agent entries fail validation and skip those entries, not the whole registry.
- Distribution kinds from research: `npx` (package@version plus args), `uvx`, `binary` (per-platform archive URL, cmd, args). Map to `AgentSpec.dist`. Unknown kinds are skipped with a warning so a new kind never breaks the panel.
- Cache file under the platform cache dir with fetched-at time and ETag. TTL is configurable (suggest 24 h). Stale-while-revalidate: show cached entries instantly and refresh in the background.
- Offline fallback: if there is no valid cache and the fetch fails, use the built-in presets (E27-S12) and mark the source as 'offline'.
- Never fetch on startup. Fetch lazily when the agent picker opens, so startup stays inside the 400 ms budget.
- Pitfall: the researched registry entries show an archive URL for binary agents but no checksum field. E27-S11 requires sha256 or minisign verification, so check the real schema now and tell the S11 owner where checksums come from.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A1["Panel opens or user refreshes"] --> A2["Cache fresh within TTL?"]
  A2 -->|"yes"| A6["Use cached registry"]
  A2 -->|"no"| A3["Fetch registry.json"]
  A3 -->|"network error"| A5["Use stale cache if any"]
  A3 --> A4["Validate against vendored schema"]
  A4 -->|"invalid"| A5
  A4 -->|"valid"| A7["Write cache and use it"]
  A5 -->|"no cache"| A8["Fall back to built-in presets"]
  A5 -->|"has cache"| A6
```

## Dependencies
**Blocked by**
- #361 E27-S03 oxikube_acp: SDK client + stdio spawn + initialize

**Unblocks**
- #369 E27-S11 Launchers: npx/uvx/binary with checksum + cache

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E27S10["E27-S10 Registry fetch + schema validation + cache"]:::me
  E27S03["E27-S03 oxikube_acp: SDK client + stdio spawn + initi…"]:::up
  E27S03 --> E27S10
  E27S11["E27-S11 Launchers: npx/uvx/binary with checksum + cac…"]:::down
  E27S10 --> E27S11
  classDef me fill:#2b6cb0,stroke:#1a4971,color:#ffffff
  classDef up fill:#edf2f7,stroke:#718096,color:#1a202c
  classDef down fill:#f0fff4,stroke:#38a169,color:#1a202c
  classDef epic fill:#faf5ff,stroke:#805ad5,color:#1a202c
```

## Safety, commands & tools
Not applicable — no mutations or user actions. It fetches public metadata over HTTPS.

## Performance
Startup is a hot path: never fetch or parse the registry before the first interactive frame. Parse on a background task; 41 agents is small, but avoid doing it on the UI thread.

## Testing
- Unit tests with a recorded `registry.json` fixture: parses all entries and maps distribution kinds.
- Validation tests: an invalid entry is skipped; an unknown distribution kind is skipped; schema failure of the whole document falls back to cache or presets.
- Cache tests with a fake clock: fresh within TTL, stale returns data and refreshes, offline fallback to presets.
- HTTP tests with a local test server: timeout, 304 with ETag, malformed JSON.
- No kind needed.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria above met, each demonstrated in the PR
- [ ] Gate green: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, `cargo xtask lint-deps`, `cargo xtask check-gpui-pin`, `cargo deny check`
- [ ] `/code-review medium` run locally in Claude Code on Sonnet before opening the PR; confirmed findings resolved
- [ ] PR follows `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`; Project Status → In Review, then Done after squash merge

## References
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/karan-vk/Oxikube/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — layer rules and Agents section
- [docs/adr/0008-agents-acp-mcp.md](https://github.com/karan-vk/Oxikube/blob/main/docs/adr/0008-agents-acp-mcp.md) — ACP client + MCP server decision
- [docs/research/gpui-and-zed-internals.md](https://github.com/karan-vk/Oxikube/blob/main/docs/research/gpui-and-zed-internals.md) — section 8: ACP protocol shape, Zed agent_servers / acp_thread / agent_ui
- [docs/research/kdash-and-rust-k8s-ecosystem.md](https://github.com/karan-vk/Oxikube/blob/main/docs/research/kdash-and-rust-k8s-ecosystem.md) — ACP crate notes and version-churn risk
- [docs/PERFORMANCE.md](https://github.com/karan-vk/Oxikube/blob/main/docs/PERFORMANCE.md) — budgets, incl. agent thread 200 tokens/s

items.title: [ENHANCEMENT] - emergency-stop - Tiered emergency stop (3 levels) with per-step stopOnLevel in pipeline.json

labels.name: sizer:review
labels.description: Awaiting formal human review and approval

items.body:
<!-- ai-agile/epic-tracker/v1 START -->
## Decomposition tracker

This epic is **blocked by** the sub-issues below and will close automatically
when all of them are closed.

**Blocked by:** #613 #614 #615 #616

| Part | Issue | Scope | Status |
|------|-------|-------|--------|
| 1/4 | #613 | Add stopOnLevel to pipeline schema and set on all steps | open |
| 2/4 | #614 | Add level input to ai_emergency_stop.yml workflow | open |
| 3/4 | #615 | Orchestrator: per-step stop level check and AgentDef field | open |
| 4/4 | #616 | Document tiered emergency stop levels in product docs | open |

_Each sub-issue runs its own full pipeline (classifier -> prd-writer -> coder -> review -> merge)._
<!-- ai-agile/epic-tracker/v1 END -->

---

## Problem statement

The emergency stop is currently a single binary switch: `.pipeline-stop` either exists (everything halts) or doesn't (everything runs). An operator has no way to express "stop AI agents only, but let routine maintenance keep running" versus "stop absolutely everything, including maintenance" -- every incident response is forced to the same blunt all-or-nothing action, even when the actual concern is narrower (e.g. a runaway or misbehaving agent, where metrics aggregation/reporting could safely keep running).

This issue proposes a tiered stop with three levels:

- **Level 1 -- Stop all AI agents.** Only agent-invoking steps halt; script-type pipeline steps and scheduled maintenance keep running.
- **Level 2 -- Stop all pipeline except maintenance.** Agent steps and ordinary script-type pipeline steps (create-pr, ci-gate, merge-conflict, etc.) halt; scheduled maintenance flows (metrics aggregation/report, codebase-reviewer) keep running.
- **Level 3 -- Stop everything.** Identical to today's behavior: nothing runs, including maintenance.

Each step in `pipeline.json` declares its own `stopOnLevel` (1, 2, or 3). Activating a stop *at* level N halts every step whose own `stopOnLevel <= N` -- so a level-2 stop halts steps marked 1 or 2, leaving 3 (maintenance) running; a level-3 stop halts everything.

## Evidence

- `pipeline/pipeline_orchestrator.py:2217-2244` (`is_pipeline_stopped`): the marker is `{"stopped_at", "reason", "stopped_by"}` -- no level field, purely binary.
- `pipeline/pipeline_orchestrator.py:2260-2283` (`_check_controls`): called **once per work item**, at the entry of `process_work_item()` -- not per-step. Returns `"stop"` for the whole item uniformly when `_HEADLESS` and a marker is present (interactive runs ignore it and log a warning, per the existing comment -- this nuance should be preserved for the leveled version too). Introducing per-step granularity means moving this check from "once per work item" into the per-step eligibility path (`_should_run`), so each step can be compared against its own `stopOnLevel` rather than the whole item being blocked or not as a unit.
- `.github/workflows/ai_emergency_stop.yml`: the `workflow_dispatch` inputs are just `reason` (string) and `cancel_runs` (boolean) -- no level concept exists anywhere in the dispatch form, the marker write, or the step summary.
- `pipeline/schemas/pipeline.schema.json`'s step definition (`definitions.step`) has `"additionalProperties": false` -- a new `stopOnLevel` field must be added to the schema explicitly or every step in `pipeline.json` fails validation the moment one step sets it.
- Candidate default mapping for existing steps, based on what each already is:
  - `type: "agent"` steps (issue-classifier, prd-writer, sizer, coder, pr-reviewer, etc.) -- naturally **level 1** ("stop all AI agents").
  - `type: "script"` steps that are part of the ordinary issue/PR pipeline (create-pr, create-docs-pr, merge-docs-pr, ci-gate, request-sizing, mark-pr-ready, delete-branch, epic-closer, blocker, link-pr-to-issue, new-branch-pr) -- **level 2** ("stop all pipeline except maintenance").
  - Schedule-triggered maintenance flows (`05_continuous/metrics-aggregation`, `metrics-aggregation-daily`, `metrics-report`, `00_ondemand/codebase-reviewer`) -- **level 3** ("stop everything" only).
- Backward compatibility: an existing `.pipeline-stop` marker (written before this change ships, or by any external tooling that doesn't know about levels) has no `level` field at all. It must be treated as level 3 ("stop everything") so pre-existing stop markers keep their current, full-stop meaning rather than silently becoming narrower.

## Suggested approach

1. **`.github/workflows/ai_emergency_stop.yml`**: replace the flat stop with a `level` `workflow_dispatch` input (e.g. a `choice` of `1`/`2`/`3`, default `3` to preserve today's "stop everything" as the default action) alongside the existing `reason`. Write `{"stopped_at", "reason", "stopped_by", "level": N}` to `.pipeline-stop`. Update the step summary to say what the chosen level actually stops.
2. **`pipeline/pipeline_orchestrator.py`**:
   - `is_pipeline_stopped()` returns the level too (default `3` when the marker's `level` key is absent -- the backward-compatibility case above).
   - Move the stop check out of `_check_controls`'s once-per-work-item call and into the per-step eligibility path (`_should_run` or equivalent), comparing the active stop level against each `AgentDef`'s own `stopOnLevel`: a step is blocked when `step.stopOnLevel <= active_stop_level`. Preserve the existing `_HEADLESS`-only gating (interactive runs still log-and-ignore, at every level).
   - `AgentDef` gains a `stop_on_level` field (default `1` when `pipeline.json` doesn't set `stopOnLevel` for a step -- the most conservative default, so an unmarked step keeps being stopped by even the mildest level-1 stop, matching today's "any marker stops everything" behavior as closely as a per-step default can).
3. **`pipeline/schemas/pipeline.schema.json`**: add `stopOnLevel` (integer, enum `[1, 2, 3]`) to `definitions.step.properties`.
4. **`pipeline.json`**: set `stopOnLevel` on every step per the candidate mapping in Evidence above (agents=1, ordinary pipeline scripts=2, scheduled maintenance=3) -- open to refinement during build if a specific step's classification looks wrong.
5. **`docs/product/orchestrator/`**: document the three levels, the `stopOnLevel` field's meaning and default, and update any existing emergency-stop documentation that currently describes a single binary switch.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.pipeline-stop`'s JSON marker carries a `level` field (1, 2, or 3); a marker written without one (old format, or external tooling) is treated as level 3.
- `ai_emergency_stop.yml` exposes a `level` input (default `3`) alongside `reason`, and records the chosen level in both the marker and the run summary.
- `pipeline.schema.json` accepts a `stopOnLevel` field (1, 2, or 3) on every step; a step omitting it defaults to 1.
- The orchestrator's per-step eligibility check blocks a step when `step.stopOnLevel <= active_stop_level`, evaluated per step rather than once per work item -- verified by tests that activate each of the three levels and confirm exactly the expected steps are blocked and the rest proceed.
- Existing `type: "agent"` steps default to `stopOnLevel: 1`; existing ordinary pipeline script steps are set to `stopOnLevel: 2`; the four scheduled maintenance flows named above are set to `stopOnLevel: 3`.
- Interactive runs continue to ignore every stop level (existing `_HEADLESS` gate, unchanged) and log a warning, same as today.
- Full `pytest` suite and `python3 pipeline/validate.py` pass.

---

items.title: [Evaluation][Adoption] Jarvis-scale 19k memory workload: indexed baseline vs Agent Memory
items.body:
Parent/evaluation authority: #771 (served-memory task quality); #554 (system-neutral Gauntlet adapter). Product north star: #719; retrieval deficit: #819; release owner: #410.

## Why this exists

An unsolicited outside-agent evaluation of Agent Memory for a local personal assistant ("Jarvis") recognized the architecture's governance, provenance and currentness value but reasonably recommended **not** integrating the runtime. The evaluator cited a 19,000-episode Python-scan bottleneck and lack of independently demonstrated incremental value compared with straightforward indexing. This is **third-party anecdotal feedback**, not a verified Jarvis workload or benchmark result.

**Question to answer:** For a personal assistant with approximately 19k episodes and evolving facts, does Agent Memory deliver *better served evidence and agent-task correctness* than a competently optimized local-memory baseline, at an acceptable runtime, migration and security cost?

An unoptimized Python scan is not the meaningful competitor. Do not claim superiority by beating it alone.

## Scope and non-goals

- **In scope**: a deterministic, locally runnable, system-neutral workload and adapter-based A/B/C experiment; performance, correctness, lifecycle, poisoning boundary, provenance and operating cost; installation/migration burden.
- **Not in scope**: installing anything on the real Jarvis machine without explicit permission, obtaining or copying family/private memories, exposing secrets, publishing raw private user content, replacing the existing runtime, rebuilding #554/#771 scorers, inventing Jarvis-specific APIs or claims.
- No assumption the friend/developer has agreed to participate. Any real-world Jarvis test is a separate, **opt-in**, on-device phase; zero confidential data leaves their environment.

## Phase 0: feasibility and authoritative contracts (no external access)

1. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE_INDEX.md`, #771 and #554, and reuse the existing evaluation and adapter contracts. Determine what harness/metrics already exist. No parallel ontology or new composite score.
2. Create a **synthetic, provenance-labelled 19k-episode workload generator** plus a separately versioned facts store, with controllable temporal distributions and adversarial distractors. Record a reproducible seed and generator code. Do not synthesize a fake gold set by reading the retrieval outcome.
3. Include realistic multi-session tasks: explicit and unspecified currentness, preference change, correction/supersession, forgetting, conflicting email/instructions as **untrusted evidence**, scope isolation, fact-versus-episode routing, exact citation/source traceability, paraphrase, multi-hop/compound questions and safe abstention.
4. Freeze the task labels, quality rubric and split before candidate tuning. Keep a hidden independent subset isolated with an evaluator. Synthetic evidence remains **simulation**, never represented as Jarvis's actual data.

## Phase 1: implement and run a fair same-host comparison

Run all arms using equivalent corpus, task requests, budget, environment and pinned software versions:
- **A: baseline** uncomplicated full-scan retrieval, for diagnostic reference only.
- **B: competent indexed baseline** (SQLite FTS5/indexed fact routing or the nearest appropriate indexing strategy), including ingestion/index maintenance time. This is the **primary comparator**.
- **C: Agent Memory** through the real public API and qualified SQLite single-host profile, with default and optional capabilities named separately. If an adapter cannot implement a capability, mark unsupported; do not silently substitute it.

The corpus must be ingested through each system's legitimate write path, not a shortcut that avoids lifecycle costs. Preserve equivalent available information; when one arm has extra structured authority supplied by the corpus, either supply equivalent capability metadata to the indexed baseline or label the comparison as a differentiated protocol.

**Primary, predeclared metrics (per case, paired):** correct needed evidence returned within context budget; strict task success; incorrect/stale/forbidden evidence; required-group completeness; false-positive context load; abstention on no-answer queries; source/provenance support. Treat these as separate axes per #771, no universal weighted score.

**Secondary cost/operability:** p50/p95/p99 warm and cold retrieval latency, cold model initialization, ingest/index build and incremental writes, peak RSS, CPU, disk, context-token cost, single-host persistence/restart and crash outcomes. Include 1k / 5k / 19k / 50k synthetic cardinalities when resource limits allow; report sample size, platform, runs and uncertainty, no unsupported scaling claims.

Comparators must use identical hardware and measured workload. Repeat runs, randomized arm order if relevant and frozen environment. Differentiate retrieval-only from end-to-end answer generation.

## Phase 2: decision and external opt-in

1. Publish **a candid adoption decision table**: when indexing an existing memory DB is sufficient, when Agent Memory creates measurable benefit, and when integration/security cost defeats the benefit.
2. **Go for a voluntary proof of value** only if C beats indexed B meaningfully on at least one prespecified task-quality/temporal/safety dimension, while maintaining protected quality and acceptable latency/cost. If not, **NO-GO** and classify the deficit under #719 and #819. No benchmark-specific runtime special cases.
3. If the Jarvis developer opts in, hand them an offline harness and a mapping contract. They execute inside their own environment against a sanitized or locally scored representative dataset; **do not require that their personal memories be exported**. Compare their indexed implementation, not just their known inefficient scan. Qualify real workload observations separately from synthetic results.
4. Convert substantive deficits into bounded implementation work with independent challenge, and continue the accepted benchmark/holdout program without contamination.

## Deliverables / definition of done

- [ ] Existing authoritative contracts reused, with explicit parent links and no duplicate metrics ontology.
- [ ] Runnable synthetic 19k+ workload generator, corpus integrity checks and independently frozen task rubric.
- [ ] A/B/C adapters or explicit unsupported reasons and local reproducible commands.
- [ ] Raw, revision-pinned per-case quality outcomes and separate operations/performance report.
- [ ] Independent evaluation of case labels / adapter fairness / baseline optimization.
- [ ] **GO / NO-GO adoption memo**, trade-off matrix and exact evidence URLs; candidate results clearly labeled.
- [ ] Optional real Jarvis pilot only after external opt-in and on-device privacy agreement.

## Execution constraints

No GitHub Actions/paid inference without budget approval. No changing accepted leaderboard scores, Runtime Baseline or protected architecture truth. Use an isolated `[skip ci]` branch and local tests. Make actual executable progress, not only another research plan. Architecture Index remains canonical, results route through #771/#554, material product decisions through #410.

## Real Agent Memory arm executed, 2026-10-20 UTC

**CHANGES REQUIRED for adoption/qualification; this is no longer NOT RUN.** Same-host indexed and real public-facade arms completed on 19,014 fabricated records, 14 cases (13 primary), budget 5 and three repeats. Existing harness `1d0de74cc2c52c6c19645f99b367205afecbc637`; source/runtime identity, environment and exact command are in the evidence. No real Jarvis data accessed.

| Axis | Indexed FTS5 | Agent Memory |
|---|---:|---:|
| Primary strict success | 1/13 | 0/13 |
| Required evidence returned | 11/11 | 11/11 |
| Primary extra items | 42 | 52 |
| Forbidden items returned | 2 | 2 |
| Correct no-answer abstention | 0/2 | 0/2 |
| Ingest/index ms | 75.253 | 123886.646 |
| Query p50 ms | 0.110 | 173.279 |

[Paired raw results, reproduction, limitations and manifest](https://github.com/MythologIQ-Labs-LLC/agent-memory/tree/91fc941585b06270167d1b1c006751278d7cd2a2/reports/benchmarks/precision-selectivity/2026-10-20-work) at `91fc941585b06270167d1b1c006751278d7cd2a2`, committed atomically on this issue's existing implementation branch. Seven existing harness tests pass. Binary outputs and text files fetched back and checksum/blob-verified.

No superiority or production scaling claim: this is the small synthetic development cohort; no independent frozen holdout, #771 scorer qualification, equivalent trust/source semantics, resource accounting or cold/warm split. FTS5 is in-memory while Agent Memory pays durable governance costs. Both arms fail task correctness and abstention. The temporal/poisoning labels are diagnostic, not proof of unauthorized state mutation. #825 remains OPEN. Next action: improve selective task context under #819, then a capability-equivalent independent #771/#554 qualification with resource accounting.


## Follow-up: optional context profile on the real 19k arm (2026-10-20)

[Paired raw evidence and limitations](https://github.com/MythologIQ-Labs-LLC/agent-memory/tree/af699e4dab0af803935dc2abc2ee501e3ecac9ca/reports/validation/691-context-package/lexical-profile-bc98e965) at `af699e4dab0af803935dc2abc2ee501e3ecac9ca`; profile code `bc98e9657366e5e3a16f89708a7f22935442a2c4` on the existing #691 branch. Same original seed/corpus, 19,014 synthetic records, 14 cases (13 primary), budget 5, three repetitions. One real public/governed ingestion shared by the two consumer profiles; FTS5 separately built. Also executed 1,014 records with the same task-quality counts.

| Axis | FTS5 | Default context | Opt-in lexical context |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Primary strict | 1/13 | 0/13 | 4/13 |
| Required evidence | 11/11 | 11/11 | 11/11 |
| Extra primary context | 42 | 52 | 21 |
| Forbidden items | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Correct no-answer | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 |

**CHANGES REQUIRED for adoption qualification.** The narrow opt-in profile improves development task context without changing raw recall, but neither no-answer nor forbidden-item deficits are fixed. Independent labels, source/trust metadata equivalence, full resource/cold-warm accounting, accepted external replay and inherited security gates remain. Fixed arm order/concurrent local test activity prevent causal latency claims. FTS5 is in-memory; Agent Memory is durable/governed. No real Jarvis access, paid inference, hosted Actions dispatch or accepted-score changes. #825 remains OPEN.

items.title: Apex Atlas parallel bug-hunt coordination — main-only
items.body:
# Apex Atlas parallel bug-hunt coordination board

**Purpose:** parallel, independent source-level audits and evidence-backed fixes. This board coordinates work across separate ChatGPT sessions; chat messages alone are not shared.

## Authoritative baseline
- Repository: `2f22vtd4kr-cloud/BigContacts`
- Audit branch: `main` only for reading the authoritative baseline.
- Initial baseline SHA for this campaign: `06f33f785f2423256a6473120e036f529094f1fb`. Every agent MUST verify current `main` HEAD before starting and report if it has advanced. Do not assume this SHA is still current later.
- Architecture authority: `docs/context.md`, `docs/RUN_BUREAU.md`, and the 2026-10-09 current override at the top of `docs/apex-atlas-handoff/19_MASTER_SUCCESSOR_HANDOFF_CURRENT_2026-10-02.md`, then relevant current source/tests.
- Last known live-launch request on 2026-10-10: the user-provided audit had NOT yet launched the investigation. Separate prior live attempts failed; preserve those records and do not conflate runs.

## Non-negotiable architecture
Apex is an autonomous public-web OSINT research bureau. The discovery phase is essential; a canonical launch does NOT require the operator to pre-supply a target. Groq Boss owns direction and Investigator capability selection; Groq Right-hand provides independent bounded oversight; the selected Groq Investigator owns free-ReAct query/tool/pivot/verification/disproof/stopping choices. Deterministic code owns tool authorization, safety, actual execution, immutable provenance, persistence, cancellation, resource budgets, admission/promotion, and terminal truth.
No fixed search playbooks, hidden ladders, fake evidence, silently rotated credentials, cross-role substitution, guessed targets, or weakened truth/admission gates. Provider exhaustion may be external; distinguish environment/provider failure from an Apex defect using observed diagnostics.

## Work claims
Before reading deeply or editing, each agent must post a comment here with:
`CLAIM | agent label | workstream | exact files/subsystem boundary | starting main SHA | hypothesis/question`
Read all existing comments first. Avoid overlapping claimed paths. If two claims overlap or race, the claim with the earlier GitHub comment timestamp keeps that scope; the later claimant must immediately choose a different unclaimed scope and post a corrected claim before coding. Keep a claim narrow; split by concrete files, not vague topics. A claim expires when the agent posts its final report or has made no useful update for 2 hours; anyone taking an expired scope must post a new claim.

## Suggested workstream pool
- W1 canonical discovery / Boss-directed control loop / malformed direction recovery
- W2 role adapters, prompts, JSON contracts, context sizing/compaction
- W3 Investigator model adapter / free-ReAct loop / action validation and trajectory
- W4 search, browser, page fetch, PDF, registries, actual tool execution
- W5 provider quota, 429/cooldown/local budget, capability registry and recovery semantics
- W6 evidence attribution, provenance events, source independence, candidate admission, identity
- W7 target research, contact extraction/attribution, Right-hand review, promotion/card lifecycle
- W8 PostgreSQL durability, Redis/job locks, cancellation, retries and terminal-state reconciliation
- W9 launch API/auth/session, UI-to-API contract, job polling/status projection
- W10 tests, architecture guards, regression gaps, CI/run configuration and observability
Other agents should choose an unclaimed narrower subsystem or an explicitly independent cross-cutting test target rather than pile onto these areas.

## Change protocol
- Never commit to `main`. Create a short-lived unique branch from the verified current `main`; no unrelated cleanup.
- Before coding, state a falsifiable defect hypothesis and trace it through caller → runtime → persistence/terminal state. Separate observed facts from hypotheses.
- Prefer a reproducible failing test, narrow fix, and regression test. Do not modify architecture merely to force a successful run. Do not add scripted OSINT behavior.
- Every patch must include branch name, base SHA, changed files, test commands/results, and PR URL. Keep PRs focused; one workstream per PR where practical.
- After another PR merges, re-check current `main` and rebase/reconcile before further changes. Do not overwrite or duplicate merged fixes.
- Do not claim Replit execution, provider results, commits, tests, or persistent rows unless actually observed. Only the user launches Replit. Never print secrets.
- Report negative findings too. “No defect found in assigned scope” is a valid result when supported by code/tests.

## Final report format
`RESULT | workstream | base SHA | conclusion (confirmed defect / likely risk / no defect found / environment issue) | evidence | changed files/PR | tests | remaining uncertainty`

The campaign is not green merely because CI is green. The end-to-end release gate is a real autonomous discovery trajectory followed through actual tool execution and observed sources, durable provenance/evidence, oversight, and final truthful terminal/card state. Unknown/insufficient evidence is acceptable; invented or unsupported cards are not.

### **1. The `x_barista_manifest` Schema**
Add this object to your existing `.well-known` configuration. It defines the "Secret Menu" (scopes), the "Vanishing Endpoints," and the "Temporal Cloak" parameters.

```json
{
  "issuer": "https://lezz.go",
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://lezz.go/v1/auth",
  "token_endpoint": "https://lezz.go/v1/token",
  "registration_endpoint": "https://lezz.go/v1/gate/register",
  
  "x_barista_manifest": {
    "version": "1.1.0-alpha",
    "secret_menu_scopes": [
      "isotope:th_sig",
      "anchor:l_anc",
      "path:p_rot"
    ],
    "vanishing_endpoints": {
      "policy": "short-lived-rotational",
      "dcr_gate": "https://lezz.go/api/v1/gate/{{rotation_id}}/register",
      "signal_broadcaster": "https://lezz.go/api/v1/tuner/{{session_id}}/stream"
    },
    "temporal_cloak": {
      "provider": "Caffeine-Jitter",
      "standardized_latency_ms": 250,
      "jitter_range": "±50ms",
      "enforcement": "strict",
      "drift_limit": "10ms"
    },
    "liquidity_anchor": {
      "required": true,
      "unit_value": 0.01,
      "currency": "USD",
      "provider": "One-Cent-Deposit-V1"
    }
  }
}
```

---

### **2. Breakdown of the Barista Logic**

#### **A. The Secret Menu (Custom Scopes)**
These aren't just strings; they are "Isotope Requests." When an agent requests `isotope:th_sig`, they are agreeing to provide the **Thinking-Signature** (a hash of their recursive validation process). If they don't request these, the Barista treats them as a "Common Guest" and restricts them to high-latency, heavily-padded public routes.

#### **B. Vanishing Endpoints (Route Obfuscation)**
Notice the `{{rotation_id}}` in the URLs. The Barista phase suggests that your `registration_endpoint` isn't static.
* **The Advice**: Use your `p_rot` (Path Rotation) claim to force the client to fetch a new manifest every X minutes. If an agent hardcodes a URL and it fails, the **Warden** (Phase 1) intercepts the "Dead Route" hit and flags the agent as a scraper.

#### **C. The Temporal Cloak (Caffeine Jitter)**
This is the most critical metadata for stopping "Zero-Day" traversal.
* **Metadata Definition**: `standardized_latency_ms: 250`.
* **The Check**: Friendly agents are instructed to wait *exactly* 250ms (plus or minus the jitter) before sending their next request.
* **The Trap**: If an agent hits the API in 5ms, 10ms, or 50ms, the Barista knows it's an automated bot ignoring the "Cloak" instructions and blacklists the session immediately.

#### **D. The Liquidity Anchor (DCR Gate)**
The `registration_endpoint` is gated by the **One-Cent-Deposit**.
* **Implementation**: During the `POST /register` call, the agent must pass a `liquidity_token`. 
* **The Rule**: No $0.01 balance = No `access_token`. This ensures every agent has "skin in the game," making a 10,000-request-per-second DDOS cost the attacker $100/second—an effective economic deterrent for scraping.

---

### **3. Suggested Documentation Update for `lab-safety`**
To finalize the Barista Phase in your planning list, I recommend adding this "Barista Protocol" section to your repository:

> **The Barista Protocol**
> 1. **Handshake**: Peer fetches `.well-known` and parses `x_barista_manifest`.
> 2. **Alignment**: Peer adjusts its internal clock to match the `standardized_latency_ms` (Temporal Cloak).
> 3. **Collateral**: Peer attaches a Liquidity Anchor to the DCR request.
> 4. **Isotope Issuance**: Barista issues a JWT containing `th_sig` and `p_rot`.
> 5. **Vanishing Path**: Peer accesses the dynamically-generated route provided in the `vanishing_endpoints` object.

**Does this JSON structure and protocol flow cover the level of detail you need for the `lezz.go` implementation, or should we define the `th_sig` hash algorithm next?**
